questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was crucial for my choosing of study destination that it wouldn't be too far away from my family and that I could see myself living there for a period of time.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I think it was a really good and learning experience. I would recommend it to everyone.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was not the easiest, but it all worked out. Talk to some of the other Erasmus students or your contact person at the hosting university, because anyone will help.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was called into a meeting with my contact person at the hosting university.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The orientation could have worked better. Be prepared to seek the information needed yourself and then people will gladly help.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I started to look for housing at a good time to find something not too overpriced; I would recommend doing the same. There are a lot of housing opportunities, but it is more difficult to find something not too expensive. Look on airbnb and talk to someone who has been on exchnage there before if you know any.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It probably is a bit more expensive, but I liked it a lot. It was nice to choose your roommates for yourself. But it depends on which experience you want.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I found the registration process at my host institution could have been more structured. I would recommend to write to your contact person when you arrive to get the information you need in the beginning to you don't miss any deadlines or meetings.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: My roommate got an email about a meeting with our contact person which I attended with her. We got information on how to go forward at that meeting.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Our contact person helped us with what we should do.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I attended all the classes I wanted. Just write directly to the professors of the class you want to attend, and they will be helpful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The regitration can be a bit chaotic at the beginning, but it will all work out and everyone you ask for help wille help you.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses differed. The levels of the courses were very different, some were quite "easy" and one of my courses was more demanding than what I first thought.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style was somewhat the same, but there was less interaction with the students during the classes, because some of the classes were big (many students).

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Languages of the Media
Digital Society
Advanced Industrial Organisation 
Data Analysis
Economic Ethics and Corporate Social Responsibility

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend Languages of the Media and Digital Society because professor Christopher Andersen was a good teacher, and the course materials were interesting. 
I would also recommend Data Analysis. It was well structured.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I did not have any unexpected costs.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Train tickets were more expensive than expected and some grocery stores were more expensive. Cheap to go out for a pasta and a glass of wine though.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
There were some walks around Milan and trips to different places in Italy. 
There were also some get to know each other activities with drinks.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend going to the get-to-know each other events at the beginning of the semester to meet some of the other Erasmus students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would recommend taking the train to Bologna. There are some cheap train tickets, and it is only 2 hours from Milan.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I found it very easy. I got a very good impression of the people in Milan, they were very welcoming.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just be open and take the initiative to talk to them in class. They will also be helpful with the material in the courses and so on.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The Italians take things more calmly, and everything goes more slowly. It can be a bit stressful in the beginning, but when you just accept that things are not as structured it is okay.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Cheap coffee, wine, and pasta. And the people are nice.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be patient and ask for help if you are confused about something. Go to different areas in the city, they differ a lot and the city has a lot to offer.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Arrive at least a week before your semester starts to get registered and settled before the courses start.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To live in a new country and make new friends. Every Erasmus student I met was open and sweet and everyone is there to get the best experience.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Not to get stressed about how unstructured the school system seemed.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
